title: ML-guided PtFeCu nanocatalyst shows enhanced oxygen-reduction activity and durability
summary: A first-principles database and neural-network-potential search explored 396,862 Pt–Fe–Cu nanoparticle configurations and mapped candidate compositions. The team synthesized PtFeCu variants and measured oxygen-reduction reaction (ORR) performance. A tested PtFeCu formulation showed about 3.1-fold higher specific activity (776 μA cm⁻² Pt) and 3.2-fold higher mass activity (0.67 A mg⁻¹ Pt) than Pt/C at 0.9 V; the authors attribute activity and improved durability to Cu-dependent surface-strain modulation and reduced Fe segregation, supported by calculations and experimental tests.
ai_technology: DFT-integrated neural-network potentials and machine-learning configuration search
organization: Yonsei University; Korea Institute of Energy Research; Hyundai Motor Company

evidence.tested: A first-principles database and neural-network-potential search explored 396,862 Pt–Fe–Cu nanoparticle configurations and mapped candidate compositions.
evidence.unknown: The result is a PtFeCu catalyst-composition/configuration finding, not a claim that the ternary system itself was previously unknown. The paper labels the high-/low-Cu variants inconsistently between its abstract/results and conclusion, so the quoted activity values are not tied here to a disputed variant name. Activity was measured in O2-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 using a rotating-disk setup; durability used a 30,000-cycle accelerated stress test, not a full fuel-cell operating lifetime. The reported 2 g batch capacity is a synthesis-scale result, not commercial manufacturing validation.
evidence.ai_role: The authors built neural-network potentials from first-principles data, screened 396,862 PtFeCu nanoparticle configurations, and used the predicted ternary configuration/composition map to guide experimental synthesis and selection of catalyst variants. The model-supported search was used to identify composition-dependent ORR activity and stability relationships; measurements and physical interpretation were performed by the research team.
